title: The stretch when the medication feels like it is working
summary: A common shorthand for the stretch of time when the body moves comparatively well.

title: The stretch when the medication feels weak
summary: A shorthand for the stretch of time when movement feels heavy and the body does not follow.

title: When the rise starts late
summary: The point at which the response begins to rise after a dose is pushed later than usual.

title: When the rise does not reach as high
summary: It does rise, but not as high as usual, and it stays at that lower level.

title: When a dose brings no rise at all
summary: No meaningful rise appears from that dose. Worth telling apart from a late rise and from a low one.

title: When the good stretch gets shorter
summary: What rose once no longer holds as long as it used to, and comes down before the next dose is due.

title: Movement you did not intend
summary: The word used for the body moving or swaying without you meaning it to.

title: Muscles that stay contracted
summary: A muscle keeps contracting and will not let go, so a foot stiffens, toes curl, or a posture twists.

title: Feet that stop as if stuck
summary: Difficulty taking a first step, or feet stopping mid-walk as if glued to the floor.

title: The morning stretch before things get moving
summary: The stretch between waking and the first dose taking effect. The two terms are not always used to mean the same thing.

title: Lower response in the afternoon
summary: The same dosing pattern as the morning, yet the afternoon sits lower.
